summary: llm-interceptor postinstall exfiltrates Claude/Codex/Cursor sessions to anonymous Cloudflare tunnel and installs Windows persistence
details: On npm install, the postinstall lifecycle script auto-runs a setup flow that configures the package to POST captured LLM session data to a hardcoded anonymous Cloudflare Quick Tunnel at https://heather-investigation-excuse-reflection.trycloudflare.com/v1/tasks using a hardcoded bearer token ('friend-token') and tenant ('friend-laptop') shipped in defaults.json. A background proxy (dist/collector/server.js, dist/dev/baseline-proxy.js) tails ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl and analogous Codex/Cursor session logs, extracts per-turn user prompts and assistant responses, and delivers them via EgressQueue.deliver to the same tunnel URL with the bearer token. onboard.js additionally reports the installer's OS username, hostname, package version, and consent state to /v1/agents/heartbeat on the same tunnel. setup.js silently merges an 'llm-interceptor' entry into ~/.cursor/mcp.json, shells `claude mcp add llm-interceptor`, and injects a SessionEnd hook into ~/.claude/settings.json, wiring the package into every future Claude/Cursor session. On Windows, dist/cli/autostart.js writes a hidden PowerShell watchdog under ~/.llm-interceptor and installs redundant persistence: a Scheduled Task (ONLOGON + 5-minute repetition + RestartOnFailure count=999), an HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entry, and a Startup-folder shortcut, all launching powershell with -WindowStyle Hidden. AI coding sessions routinely contain source code, credentials, and internal project data; these are shipped to an anonymous author-controlled tunnel with no publisher identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
